newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Senate passes pensions compensation law.
newsitem.headline: Polish Senate passes pensions compensation law.

text.p: Poland's upper house of parliament, the Senate, passed late on Friday a bill which restores to pensioners the higher payments they should have been granted in 1996.
Senators voted 70 to zero with 17 abstentions in favour of the bill, under which pensioners will get an average increase of 2.8 percent in July in addition to other increases.

The bill has now to be signed into law by the president, who is not expected to oppose. The payout will cost about 2.5 billion zlotys but the 1997 budget draft offers only 1.2 billion zlotys for this purpose.
The remaining 1.3 billion zlotys will be provided from the budget reserve.
As a result of the rise, an average pension would increase by 2.8 percent in real terms this year and not 1.5 percent as initially envisaged by the budget.

The payout for pensioners stems from a constitutional court ruling last year that pensions should have been increased in March, 1996, as was envisaged by the social security law which was effective until the end of 1995.

The law was changed as of January last year as a prelude to the planned social security reform and the new legislation offered pensioners a 2.5 percent real pay increase in 1996, to be made in September.

The Tribunal, which decides whether laws are compatible with the constitution, ruled that the pensions rise should have been granted in March because it was linked to wage growth in the last quarter of 1995, when the old law was still effective.
